newsitem.title: VIETNAM: Vietnam coffee traders sit back after busy week.
newsitem.headline: Vietnam coffee traders sit back after busy week.

text.p: Trade in Vietnam's robusta coffee came to a virtual halt on Friday after a busy week of continued price volatility, dealers said.
Farmers in the highlands of Dak Lak province, the main growing area, sold heavily earlier in the week, but were reported to be holding back stock on Friday after price falls on international markets.

"It's gone back to being boring," said one trader. "The farmers sold pretty much all they needed to by Tet (last month's Lunar New Year festival). Now they're just sitting back and playing the market."
Dealers quoted a wide range of prices, with offers at around $1,340 a tonne and bids at $1,200-1,250, but no trading was going on. Earlier in the week, bids as high as $1,480 were reported.

According to trade estimates, some 50,000-60,000 tonnes of coffee remains in Vietnam from the 1996/97 harvest, with around 200,000 tonnes having been sold since the official start of the season in October.
Dealers said between 5,000 and 10,000 tonnes had moved over the past few days, spurred on by the activity on markets in New York and London.
Coffee prices fell in London on Thursday and traders said they expected further losses on Friday as a correction continued.
